problem: Learning-based navigation needs costly robot-collected data (NoMaD) or supplemental robot demonstrations (HEAD). Existing egocentric trajectory predictors are unimodal, have narrow FOV, lack semantics and cannot see glass, and mostly are not deployed on robots.
motivation: Human walking data is cheap and scalable and encodes navigation commonsense, and manipulation has shown that human-only data can transfer to robots. Navigation lacks an embodiment-agnostic middle layer that says where one can walk, which sits between high-level planning and low-level locomotion.
key_idea: Train a conditional diffusion model on 5 hours of human egocentric walking data to predict multi-modal 6-DoF future trajectory distributions from a 360° color/depth/semantic visual memory plus DINOv3 video features, and deploy it zero-shot on a Unitree G1 via a receding-horizon selector.
insight: Scene context matters: removing all visual input gives the worst collision score (82.5), and removing semantics costs 5.1 points because doors and walls become indistinguishable. DINOv3 features give only a small offline gain (91.4 to 90.6 collision when removed) but nearly triple real-world interventions on glass (0.77 to 2.2/min), so offline metrics can mask real-world benefits. Hybrid 5 DDIM + 5 DDPM sampling keeps multi-modal quality at real-time speed.
method: Data: 44 sequences (300 min, >25 km) recorded by a person with a RealSense T265 (SLAM pose) and D455 (RGBD) at 20 Hz across diverse indoor/outdoor scenes. Augmented via sub-trajectories to 320k samples. Semantics from DINOv2 + Mask2Former (8 classes).

Visual Memory: a rolling buffer of RGBD+semantic frames is reprojected into a 180x360x5 egocentric panorama, encoded by a frozen spatial VAE into 8x20x8 latents, then attention-compressed to a 64-d embedding.
DINOv3 video features: frozen ViT-S/16 patch tokens (15x27x384) from the latest RGB frame, pooled by an attention adapter into 64-d to capture glass and dynamic agents.

Diffusion model: 46M-param non-autoregressive UNet with MHSA that predicts 100 future steps (5 s at 20 Hz, 6D pose). Conditioned on past trajectory, VM and video features via classifier-free guidance (10% condition dropout).

Hybrid sampling: 5 evenly skipped DDIM steps followed by 5 consecutive DDPM steps, trained with a linear noise schedule. The paper reports about 100x faster than full DDPM. About 1.7-2 Hz on a Jetson Thor.

Receding-horizon controller: samples 64 candidates, filters collisions via KD-tree on the VM point cloud, and K-Means (k=3) clusters them. Clusters are scored by popularity minus a momentum penalty and the medoid of the best is executed, with latency compensation and blending.
Deployment: chest-mounted cameras on the Unitree G1. VM and controller run on a Jetson Orin NX; the diffusion model and segmentation run on a Jetson Thor.

setting.backbone: Conditional UNet diffusion model (46M) + frozen spatial VAE + frozen DINOv3 ViT-S/16 + DINOv2/Mask2Former segmentation; trained from scratch on human data
setting.training_data: 5 hours (300 min, 25 km) of human egocentric walking data with RGBD and SLAM pose, 320k augmented samples; no robot data
setting.observation: egocentric RGBD (RealSense D455) with 360° visual memory panorama + semantics, plus SLAM pose history
setting.action_space: predicted 6-DoF future waypoint trajectories (5 s, 20 Hz) in the egocentric frame, tracked by a low-level humanoid locomotion controller

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark (VLN/ObjNav) results. Offline metrics on the authors' own human walking dataset (collision, smoothness, best-of-N ADE) and real-world G1 deployment statistics are the only results, so nothing fits the canonical benchmark list.
results: Offline, the full system reaches collision 91.4, smoothness 4.82, Best of 1 0.76 and Best of 15 0.39. On the pilot data it beats VAE-LSTM (collision 84.5) and CXA-Transformer (80.3) on collision and ADE, though not on smoothness (VAE-LSTM 9.09 vs 2.04). On the G1, 37.5 min and 1,137 m of zero-shot autonomous operation reach 96-99% autonomous time, with 0.13-0.80 interventions/min.
limitations: No goal conditioning: it provides only a navigation prior with no directed navigation, and it has no baseline comparison on the real robot.
Requires a stereo depth camera and offboard compute (Jetson Thor), running at only about 2 Hz.
Ablations and baselines use the pilot subset, and the real-world evaluation is small (37.5 min) with intervention-based statistics.
builds_on: Wang et al. 2023 panorama trajectory prediction (VAE-LSTM)
